shortDescription: The German 2027 energy contract hit another three-year high on Wednesday, as concerns over a potential winter gas shortage grew, while French and German spot contracts rose significantly due to falling wind power generation.($1 = 0.8591 euros)

children: The German 2027 energy contract hit another three-year high on Wednesday, as concerns over a potential winter gas shortage grew, while French and German spot contracts rose significantly due to falling wind power generation.
The German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) was up 1.27% to €127.50 ($148.41) per megawatt hour at 0717 GMT, its highest level since October 2023, according to LSEG data.
"The target of 77% gas storage by November 1st, I feel it's very, very optimistic, especially given the pricing right now," Kpler analyst Alessandro Armenia said.
The German contract rose through August, driven by gas prices and concerns over low levels of gas in storage ahead of the cold season.
As of September 1, underground gas caverns in Germany were 53% full, the lowest in the 15 years of records, gas storage industry association INES said.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was not traded, according to LSEG data.
The French baseload spot electricity contract (TRFRBD1) rose 12.6% to €173/MWh, its highest level since December 2024, LSEG data showed.
Although consumption and solar power are expected to remain largely stable, wind power generation in France is expected to fall by 2.8 gigawatts to 2.2 GW on Thursday.
French nuclear availability fell by one percentage point to 76% of total availability.
The German equivalent day-ahead contract (TRDEBD1) was up 34.1% to €197.20/MWh, hitting its highest level since June, the data showed.
German wind power generation is expected to more than halve to 11.2 GW, solar output is expected to rise by 2.3 GW to 14.2 GW, and consumption is expected to remain largely stable at 53.7 GW.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
was up 1% at €86.30 a metric ton.
